task: Build the approved VX Builder Core foundation as one shared guarded authoring engine for VX Shop Builder and the future VX Site Builder, reusing the existing canonical builder document, runtime and publication authorities; adapt the current Shop Builder workspace to the approved Visual First gold/graphite design, product-profile boundaries, contextual insertion and controlled 12-column resize without Wix-style freeform positioning.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The change touches the canonical authoring surface and responsive layout interactions used by every future VX Shop/Site page. Strong behavioral proof is justified, while critical finite-state/formal verification would add disproportionate cost because the slice reuses existing immutable draft/publish and runtime authorities rather than changing transactional commerce state.

deferredTechniques.reason: The interaction state space is high-dimensional and UI-driven; targeted state/adversarial matrices plus browser/runtime evidence provide a better assurance-to-cost ratio.
No new concurrent transactional or payment protocol is introduced; canonical persistence/publication authorities remain unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria: One shared VX Builder Core contract serves VX Shop Builder now and the future VX Site Builder through product profiles/capabilities rather than forks.
The existing Page document, Runtime, draft/preview/publish/rollback and capability authorities remain canonical; no second renderer, page authority or publication state is introduced.

The approved Visual First workspace is implemented: top toolbar, Library panel, live canvas and Inspector with no additional admin sidebar; Shoperation family styling uses light/ivory surfaces, graphite text and warm gold/ochre accents.
Contextual plus insertion only offers structurally valid targets and preserves Page -> Section -> Container -> Component structure.
Direct manipulation supports guarded 12-column resize with snapping and valid min/max spans; arbitrary freeform absolute positioning is not introduced.
Selected sections/components expose contextual quick operations including duplicate and delete while protected nodes remain protected.
Desktop, tablet and mobile editing keeps the existing canonical responsive authority and targeted overrides without duplicate breakpoint DOM/page authorities.
Merchant-facing terminology is product-profile driven so commerce-specific labels/capabilities do not become VX Builder Core assumptions.
Builder performance/stability and long-term editability take precedence over unrestricted styling freedom; guarded freedom is explicit in code and tests.
Existing Presets, Saved Blocks, Layers, Global Styles, history, preview and publish flows continue to work through their current authorities.
invariants: There is exactly one runtime renderer and one Page-document mutation authority for this Builder path.
VX Builder Core does not own commerce behavior, inventory, customer identity, provider integrations or publication transactions.
Shop and Site variants differ by profile/capability composition, not by forked editor engines.
Generic drag/drop and resize cannot create out-of-grid spans, arbitrary coordinates or invalid parent-child relationships.
Responsive edits are scoped to the active canonical viewport and never create a second mobile document.
Protected system nodes cannot be deleted, duplicated or illegally reparented.
The accepted Builder shell contains no extra Shoperation admin navigation sidebar.
Normal-mode UX hides technical implementation noise while advanced controls remain progressively disclosed.

alternatives.summary: Fork the current Visual Builder into separate Shop and Site editors and evolve each independently.
alternatives.reason: Duplicates interaction/runtime assumptions, creates drift and violates the accepted one-Core/two-products architecture.

alternatives.summary: Evolve the existing canonical Visual Builder into a shared VX Builder Core contract and keep Shoperation as the first product/host profile while preserving existing runtime and persistence authorities.
alternatives.reason: Reuses proven Page/runtime/publish infrastructure, minimizes blast radius and creates the correct extensibility seam for VX Site Builder.

alternatives.summary: Rewrite the Builder from scratch around a fully free canvas and migrate Shoperation later.
alternatives.reason: High regression risk, duplicates mature authorities and conflicts with guarded freedom, performance and stability priorities.

specialistReviews.finding: The generic Core must not become a second Page/runtime/publish authority and Shop/Site must not fork.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use a product-profile/interaction contract over the existing Storefront Builder authorities; no replacement runtime or persistence path.

specialistReviews.finding: Pointer resize and contextual insertion can bypass canonical responsive/grid rules or produce editor/runtime divergence.
specialistReviews.resolution: All direct manipulation resolves to existing validated Builder mutations and 12-column responsive values; no raw CSS-coordinate persistence or editor-only layout authority.

specialistReviews.finding: The approved Visual First design requires direct manipulation and contextual actions without exposing technical complexity.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep direct manipulation first, Inspector second; progressive disclosure, contextual plus controls and section quick actions are explicit acceptance criteria.

specialistReviews.finding: A feature-rich canvas can add heavy listeners, layout thrash and visual instability.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use bounded pointer interactions, existing frame geometry/runtime rendering, no unrestricted freeform DOM, and verify performance/readiness through existing gates.

challenge.scenario: A resize drag attempts to make a component span 13 columns or zero columns.
challenge.finding: Unbounded resizing can corrupt layout and responsive output.
challenge.resolution: Clamp/snap all resize results to canonical spans 1..12 and persist only validated responsive mutation values.

challenge.scenario: A user drags or inserts a component into a node whose child policy forbids it.
challenge.finding: Visual freedom could bypass the component registry and create invalid documents.
challenge.resolution: Contextual insertion/drop targets are derived from listStorefrontBuilderInsertableComponents and canonical mutation validation.

challenge.scenario: A direct manipulation on mobile silently changes desktop/tablet values.
challenge.finding: Responsive inheritance can become unpredictable and destroy accepted layouts.
challenge.resolution: Persist changes only to the active canonical viewport override and retain the existing shared Page document/responsive resolver.

challenge.scenario: Shop-specific commerce terminology and components are embedded into the shared Core.
challenge.finding: VX Site Builder would inherit irrelevant commerce assumptions and force a future fork.
challenge.resolution: Move product identity, terminology, categories and capability exposure behind an explicit Builder product profile.

challenge.scenario: The accepted visual redesign adds an admin navigation rail or shrinks the canvas enough to recreate historical zoom/overflow defects.
challenge.finding: The PO-approved workspace and canvas usability would regress.
challenge.resolution: Preserve top toolbar + Library + canvas + Inspector only, keep the existing canonical canvas geometry/fit authority, and add visual contract regressions.

challenge.scenario: Direct manipulation stores arbitrary left/top/width CSS coordinates for ordinary content.
challenge.finding: Wix-style freedom would damage responsiveness, performance and long-term editability.
challenge.resolution: Generic Core exposes guarded grid/token operations only; absolute positioning remains restricted to specialized layered components already modeled by canonical configuration.

challenge.scenario: A section preset or saved block creates a second rendering or state authority.
challenge.finding: Library convenience could diverge from runtime and publication truth.
challenge.resolution: Presets and saved blocks materialize normal canonical nodes/documents and continue through existing mutation, validation and persistence authorities.

challenge.scenario: A protected header/footer receives duplicate/delete controls.
challenge.finding: Critical navigation/shell structure could be damaged.
challenge.resolution: Quick actions remain visible only when allowed and canonical protectedSystem checks continue to block destructive mutations.

challenge.scenario: Large pages generate excessive pointer/resize state updates and degrade editing responsiveness.
challenge.finding: Builder sophistication could reduce practical usability.
challenge.resolution: Commit mutations at bounded interaction points, avoid per-frame persistence, preserve runtime rendering authority and include performance/readiness regression checks.

proofPlan: Run Plan Before Code against the exact branch before product-code execution.
Add unit coverage for VX Builder Core product profiles, guarded-freedom policy, structural hierarchy and resize normalization.
Extend Visual Builder completion regression coverage for approved shell, gold/graphite design tokens, contextual insertion, duplicate/delete and no extra admin sidebar.
Verify resize boundary cases 1/12 and 12/12 plus active viewport isolation against canonical responsive mutation behavior.
Run existing Visual Builder, Page/Runtime and Known Failure regression suites selected by Incremental Replay.
Run typecheck and production build on the exact implementation HEAD.
Run Template Factory / browser-facing quality authority where impacted to prove runtime/editor parity and responsive stability.
Run Completion Truth Gate with exact branch/SHA evidence; no DONE claim is allowed from a stale or partial run.

requirements.requirement: Implement one shared VX Builder Core foundation with product-profile composition for VX Shop Builder and future VX Site Builder, without forking editor/runtime authorities.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No second renderer, Page-document authority, publication state or separate Shop/Site editor engine is introduced.

requirements.requirement: Match the PO-approved Visual First workspace structure and Shoperation-family visual language: top toolbar, Library, live canvas, Inspector, light/ivory surfaces, graphite hierarchy and warm gold/ochre accents.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No additional Shoperation admin navigation sidebar is added to the Builder workspace.

requirements.requirement: Provide contextual insertion through valid plus/drop targets while preserving Page -> Section -> Container -> Component structural authority.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Invalid parent-child insertion cannot bypass component registry or canonical mutation validation.

requirements.requirement: Provide guarded direct 12-column resizing with snap/clamp behavior and active-viewport persistence.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Generic resizing cannot persist arbitrary freeform coordinates or grid spans outside 1..12 and cannot mutate unrelated viewports.

requirements.requirement: Keep contextual section/component quick operations including duplicate and delete, with protected-system safeguards.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Protected nodes cannot be illegally duplicated, deleted or reparented.

requirements.requirement: Preserve Desktop/Tablet/Mobile authority, responsive overrides, history, Layers, Presets, Saved Blocks, Global Styles, preview and publish workflows.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No duplicate breakpoint DOM/page authority, runtime divergence or loss of existing Builder mutation/publish capabilities.

requirements.requirement: Enforce Guarded Freedom: stability, storefront speed and long-term editability outrank unrestricted Wix-style configuration.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No unrestricted absolute positioning, raw HTML/JS composition or uncontrolled style/widget proliferation is added.

requirements.requirement: Close the slice only with fresh exact-head evidence under the new Operational Intelligence and Completion Truth Gate.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No main merge, golden update or gate weakening occurs as a side effect of this implementation.

notes: PO-approved Visual First authority is fixed for this slice. Implement by evolving the current canonical Visual Builder v3 and introducing shared VX Core/profile seams; do not rewrite or fork the editor. The large visual Section/Preset library framework may be made Core-ready now, but broad preset population remains aligned with the accepted template-portfolio sequencing. No main merge and no golden update.
